fields.text: A method of using a system for making a coffee beverage, comprising steps of: providing an apparatus including a barcode reader configured to read a barcode, and being adapted to supply heated water under pressure, the apparatus including a mandrel; loading a first portion capsule into the apparatus, the first portion capsule including a first lid that is sealed to a base element having a cavity within which a powdered coffee material is located, the base element has been shaped to define (1) a wall (a) that defines the cavity with a central interior portion, and (b) having a plurality of ribs that are (1) radially spaced, (11) vertically oriented, and (iii) configured to extend toward the central interior portion and (2) a circumferential flange having a top side and a bottom side with a first barcode located on the bottom side; reading the second barcode with the barcode reader; controlling production of a second coffee beverage based upon the reading of the second barcode; introducing the heated water into the second portion capsule via the water inlet that is arranged along the central axis of the second portion capsule according to production conditions associated with the second barcode to form the second coffee beverage.

Leonhardt discloses a method of controlled release of a replacement heart valve with a collapsible stent and valve, a pusher/catheter and moveable sheath, guide wire lumen, partial deployment by retracting the sheath, and recovering the valve within the sheath, anticipating the claims.

Garrison discloses a method of controlled release of a valve replacement including a stent/valve device, delivery system with pusher/catheter and moveable sheath, partial deployment by pushing the catheter out of the sheath, and recovering the valve device within the sheath, anticipating the claims.

In the alternative, if recovery is not inherently disclosed by Garrison, it would have been obvious to move the moveable sheath to recover the valve at the point of partial expansion since Garrison discloses repositioning, making the claims obvious over Garrison alone.

Under an alternate interpretation, Garrison discloses the claimed method substantially but lacks recovering the valve within the sheath; Leonhardt teaches checking valve position after partial deployment and recovering it within the sheath if repositioning is needed, and it would have been obvious to combine Garrison's method with Leonhardt's recovery step to allow repositioning or removal if positioning is inaccurate.

Claims 9-18 and 26-29 are rejected as obvious over Kruger, which discloses a method using an apparatus and portion capsule with a barcode reader, base element with cavity and ribs, circumferential flange with barcode, mandrel piercing, and heated water introduction; repetition of steps to make additional beverages and different barcodes for different beverages found obvious.

Claims rejected as obvious over Schifferle combined with Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, and Rossi, which together disclose a capsule/apparatus system with foil lid, vertical ribs, barcode on flange bottom, barcode comparison and activation logic, and absence of a filter, motivating a combination to arrive at claimed features including second capsule use.

Claim 12 is rejected as obvious over Schifferle in view of Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, Rossi, and further in view of Rubino, which discloses vertical ribs that provide optimal conveyance of water/turbulent flow within a coffee capsule.

Claims 16 and 18 are rejected as obvious over Schifferle in view of Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, Rossi, and Mahlich, which discloses a barcode reader placed below a media chute holding capsules, enabling automatic scanning before brewing.

Claims 9 and 26 are objected to for informalities because they contain roman numerals and other non-reference-character numerals/letters enclosed in parentheses, which should only be used for reference characters.

The drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a) for failing to show every feature specified in the claims, including an apparatus adapted to supply heated water, introduction of heated water along the central axis, and sealing of the flange/foil lids against a seal of the apparatus.

The drawings are further objected to for improper numbering of partial views and for reference character '15' being used to designate two different features (an arrow in figure 2 and grooves in figures 19 and 22), in violation of 37 CFR 1.84(p)(4).

The specification is objected to for lacking proper antecedent basis for numerous method steps recited in claims 9 and 26, such as loading/unloading capsules, reading barcodes, sealing, piercing, and forming coffee beverages.

Claims 10 and 19 recite 'the portion capsule is free of a filter,' which fails the enablement requirement because it is not clear how an infusion capsule would function without some sort of filter device to retain the coffee material.
Claims 10 and 19 recite 'the portion capsule is free of a filter' which fails the written description requirement because the application does not appear to disclose this concept.
Claims 9-28 are rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
Claim 9 recites 'a base element' and 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two base elements and cavities or just one.
Claim 19 recites 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two cavities or just one.
Claim 19 recites 'the barcode reader' lacking antecedent basis, and it is unclear if this is the same element as the 'detector'.
Claim 20 recites 'an amount of water' and it is unclear whether this is the same as the 'heated water' of parent claim 19.
Claim 26 recites 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two cavities or just one.
Claim 26 recites 'the barcode reader' with insufficient antecedent basis, unclear if same as 'detector'.
Claim 26 lacks an unloading step for the first capsule, making it unclear if the apparatus must hold two capsules simultaneously.
Claims 27-28 were misnumbered as claims 26-27, and claim 27 depends from claim 25, creating ambiguity as to whether claim 27 should depend from claim 26.

Schifferle discloses a coffee-making apparatus with barcode reading, capsule loading and piercing, water introduction, and control of production conditions, but lacks a foil lid, vertical ribs, barcode on the flange bottom, comparison/activation steps, filter-free capsule, and use of a second capsule; Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, and WO 2010/099806 supply these missing features, and it would have been obvious to combine them for reasons including strengthening the capsule, protecting the barcode from damage, and ensuring proper brewing.

The base combination does not explicitly recite ribs inducing turbulent flow; EP 1849718A1 teaches vertical ribs that provide optimal conveyance of water through the capsule, and it would have been obvious to incorporate this into the Schifferle combination to ensure effective brewing.

The base combination does not explicitly recite a barcode reader placed in a media chute; Mahlich teaches such a reader below a media chute, and it would have been obvious to combine this for faster, automatic scanning of capsules.

Claims 9-28 (particularly claim 9) are provisionally rejected for nonstatutory double patenting over claims 1-9 of copending Application No. 16/438,818 in view of Schifferle and Sweeney, since the '818 application lacks a bar code reader, vertical ribs, piercing the lid, and controlling the process, which are taught by Schifferle and Sweeney.
Claim numbering objection: misnumbered claims 26-27 were renumbered as 27-28, and the original numbering must be preserved throughout prosecution per 37 CFR 1.126.

reading the first barcode with the barcode reader; controlling a production process of a first coffee beverage based upon the reading of the first barcode; piercing the first foil lid with a mandrel of the apparatus in a region that is offset from a central axis of the first portion capsule; sealing the top side of the flange and/or the first foil lid against a seal of the apparatus; introducing heated water into the first portion capsule through a water inlet of the apparatus that is arranged along the central axis of the portion capsule to form the first coffee beverage; loading a second portion capsule into the apparatus, the second portion capsule including a second foil lid sealed to a base element having a cavity within which a powdered coffee material is located, the cavity of the second portion capsule being free of a filter and including a central portion, and a plurality of ribs that are radially spaced, vertically oriented, and configured to extend toward the central portion of the cavity, the base element of the second portion capsule including a circumferential flange having a top side on which the second foil lid is sealed and an opposing bottom side with a second barcode located on the bottom side and being different from the first barcode; reading the second barcode with the barcode reader; controlling a second production process of a second coffee beverage based upon the reading of the second barcode, the second production process being different than the first production process; piercing the second foil lid with the mandrel of the apparatus in a region that is offset from a central axis of the second portion capsule; sealing the top side of the flange and/or the second foil lid of the second portion capsule against the seal of the apparatus; and introducing the heated water into the second portion capsule to form the second coffee beverage.

detecting a contact with the touch-sensitive display at a first predefined location corresponding to an unlock image;
continuously moving the unlock image on the touch-sensitive display in accordance with movement of the contact while continuous contact with the touch screen is maintained, wherein the unlock image is a graphical, interactive user-interface object with which a user interacts in order to unlock the device; and
unlocking the hand-held electronic device if the moving the unlock image on the touch-sensitive display results in movement of the unlock image from the first predefined location to a predefined unlock region on the touch-sensitive display.

Claims 5-6 and 9-10 are rejected as unpatentable over Rytivaara in view of Astheimer, because Rytivaara does not explicitly disclose a visual cue comprising text and an arrow indicating direction, but Astheimer teaches visual cues comprising arrows pointing in the right direction, and it would have been obvious to combine these as a predictable substitution of one known visual cue element for another.

fields.summary: Claims fail written description requirement; the specification does not support the combination of retracting the moveable sheath to expose a portion of the valve device AND recovering the portion within the sheath, since recovery is only disclosed with the pusher-member deployment method, not the sheath-retraction method.

Claims are indefinite because they recite 'advancing the delivery and implantation system over the guide wire' though the guide wire itself is not positively claimed, only a lumen capable of receiving a guide wire, making it unclear whether a guide wire is required.

Leonhardt discloses a method of controlled release of a replacement heart valve with a collapsible stent and valve, a pusher/catheter and moveable sheath, guide wire lumen, partial deployment by retracting the sheath, and recovering the valve within the sheath, anticipating the claims.

Garrison discloses a method of controlled release of a valve replacement including a stent/valve device, delivery system with pusher/catheter and moveable sheath, partial deployment by pushing the catheter out of the sheath, and recovering the valve device within the sheath, anticipating the claims.

In the alternative, if recovery is not inherently disclosed by Garrison, it would have been obvious to move the moveable sheath to recover the valve at the point of partial expansion since Garrison discloses repositioning, making the claims obvious over Garrison alone.

Under an alternate interpretation, Garrison discloses the claimed method substantially but lacks recovering the valve within the sheath; Leonhardt teaches checking valve position after partial deployment and recovering it within the sheath if repositioning is needed, and it would have been obvious to combine Garrison's method with Leonhardt's recovery step to allow repositioning or removal if positioning is inaccurate.

Claims 54, 60, 66, and 68 require the 'stent member to become flexible and supple' when exposed to cold temperatures, which is new matter not supported by the original specification, which instead discloses that the components (stent and valve) as a whole become flexible and supple. Claims 69-70 depend on 68 and inherit the issue.

Leonhardt discloses the claimed method of controlled release of a percutaneous replacement heart valve but does not disclose pericardial tissue specifically; Spenser teaches use of pericardial tissue as a known biological material for a valve attached to a stent, making the combination obvious as an alternate material.

Leonhardt discloses the claimed method but not pericardial tissue or valve attachment to the proximal portion of the stent; Spenser teaches pericardial tissue as a valve material and McGuckin teaches that valve placement (proximal, distal, or intermediate) are obvious alternatives, making the combination obvious.

Bessler discloses the claimed method using a self-expanding nitinol stent but does not disclose exposing the stent to cold temperatures prior to loading; Teitelbaum teaches cooling a self-expanding nitinol stent prior to loading to make it flexible and supple for easier compression, making the combination obvious.

Claims are indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention, including unclear numbering/sequencing of coffee beverage formation steps, lack of antecedent basis for 'the first foil lid' and 'the second foil lid' in claim 26, and indefiniteness of the term 'system' which mixes apparatus and method claiming.
Claims 11 and 12 are of improper dependent form because claim 11 does not further limit claim 9, since claim 9 already recites piercing the foil lids with a mandrel (i.e., providing holes).

Claims 9-18 and 26-29 are rejected as obvious over Kruger, which discloses a method using an apparatus and portion capsule with a barcode reader, base element with cavity and ribs, circumferential flange with barcode, mandrel piercing, and heated water introduction; repetition of steps to make additional beverages and different barcodes for different beverages found obvious.

Claims rejected as obvious over Schifferle combined with Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, and Rossi, which together disclose a capsule/apparatus system with foil lid, vertical ribs, barcode on flange bottom, barcode comparison and activation logic, and absence of a filter, motivating a combination to arrive at claimed features including second capsule use.

Claim 12 is rejected as obvious over Schifferle in view of Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, Rossi, and further in view of Rubino, which discloses vertical ribs that provide optimal conveyance of water/turbulent flow within a coffee capsule.

Claims 16 and 18 are rejected as obvious over Schifferle in view of Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, Rossi, and Mahlich, which discloses a barcode reader placed below a media chute holding capsules, enabling automatic scanning before brewing.

Claims 9 and 26 are objected to for informalities because they contain roman numerals and other non-reference-character numerals/letters enclosed in parentheses, which should only be used for reference characters.

The drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a) for failing to show every feature specified in the claims, including an apparatus adapted to supply heated water, introduction of heated water along the central axis, and sealing of the flange/foil lids against a seal of the apparatus.

The drawings are further objected to for improper numbering of partial views and for reference character '15' being used to designate two different features (an arrow in figure 2 and grooves in figures 19 and 22), in violation of 37 CFR 1.84(p)(4).

The specification is objected to for lacking proper antecedent basis for numerous method steps recited in claims 9 and 26, such as loading/unloading capsules, reading barcodes, sealing, piercing, and forming coffee beverages.

Claims 10 and 19 recite 'the portion capsule is free of a filter,' which fails the enablement requirement because it is not clear how an infusion capsule would function without some sort of filter device to retain the coffee material.
Claims 10 and 19 recite 'the portion capsule is free of a filter' which fails the written description requirement because the application does not appear to disclose this concept.
Claims 9-28 are rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
Claim 9 recites 'a base element' and 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two base elements and cavities or just one.
Claim 19 recites 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two cavities or just one.
Claim 19 recites 'the barcode reader' lacking antecedent basis, and it is unclear if this is the same element as the 'detector'.
Claim 20 recites 'an amount of water' and it is unclear whether this is the same as the 'heated water' of parent claim 19.
Claim 26 recites 'a cavity' twice, making it unclear whether there are two cavities or just one.
Claim 26 recites 'the barcode reader' with insufficient antecedent basis, unclear if same as 'detector'.
Claim 26 lacks an unloading step for the first capsule, making it unclear if the apparatus must hold two capsules simultaneously.
Claims 27-28 were misnumbered as claims 26-27, and claim 27 depends from claim 25, creating ambiguity as to whether claim 27 should depend from claim 26.

Schifferle discloses a coffee-making apparatus with barcode reading, capsule loading and piercing, water introduction, and control of production conditions, but lacks a foil lid, vertical ribs, barcode on the flange bottom, comparison/activation steps, filter-free capsule, and use of a second capsule; Jarisch, Sweeney, Boyd, and WO 2010/099806 supply these missing features, and it would have been obvious to combine them for reasons including strengthening the capsule, protecting the barcode from damage, and ensuring proper brewing.

The base combination does not explicitly recite ribs inducing turbulent flow; EP 1849718A1 teaches vertical ribs that provide optimal conveyance of water through the capsule, and it would have been obvious to incorporate this into the Schifferle combination to ensure effective brewing.

The base combination does not explicitly recite a barcode reader placed in a media chute; Mahlich teaches such a reader below a media chute, and it would have been obvious to combine this for faster, automatic scanning of capsules.

Claims 9-28 (particularly claim 9) are provisionally rejected for nonstatutory double patenting over claims 1-9 of copending Application No. 16/438,818 in view of Schifferle and Sweeney, since the '818 application lacks a bar code reader, vertical ribs, piercing the lid, and controlling the process, which are taught by Schifferle and Sweeney.
